deep.reconstruction:
There are no derivations, formulas or computations on this page. It is a list headed 'Preisfragen' (prize questions): candidate topics for an academy prize competition, most plausibly the Königliche Societät der Wissenschaften in Göttingen, whose mathematical class Gauss belonged to. The dating is inferred from context. The previous page holds a lunar-theory series, a ratio of true to mean lunar motion expanded in cos of combinations of E, M, a, d. The next page is dated 1816 (birth of Therese, 9 June 1816; a walk on 27 Oct 1816). So the list was probably written about 1815-1816.

The proposed topics, rendered in modern terms:
(1) The motion of an air bubble in a closed tube otherwise filled with a liquid. This is a problem of buoyancy-driven bubble motion and two-phase flow in a confined tube.
(2) 'An interesting advance in the Geometria Situs'. This is an open call for any notable progress in topology or analysis situs, in Leibniz's sense of the term.
(3) The figure (equilibrium shape) of an expansible, i.e. compressible or gaseous, fluid mass without a solid core. This is the equilibrium figure of a self-gravitating, possibly rotating, gaseous body, as opposed to the Clairaut/Laplace theory of a fluid layer on a solid nucleus.
(4) Maxima or minima in capillary action. This is a variational (energy-minimum) formulation of capillarity, i.e. deriving capillary equilibrium from a minimum principle.
(5) The perturbations of the comet of 1805. That apparition was later identified both with Encke's comet (apparition of 1805) and with Biela's comet (seen 1805); the planetary perturbations of its orbit are meant.
(6) A mathematical theory of the physical difference between air vibrations on which the specific difference of tones depends, independent of pitch and loudness. This is the difference we now call timbre (Klangfarbe). It is asked especially with regard to the articulated tones that form human speech, i.e. the vowels and the acoustics of speech sounds.

Nothing is computed. Each item is a statement of an open problem that Gauss judged worthy of a prize.

results.what: Proposal of a variational (maximum/minimum) treatment of capillary action as a prize question
results.modern_name: Variational/energy principle for capillary surfaces (Young-Laplace equation and contact-angle condition from energy minimization)
results.usually_credited_to: Young (1805) and Laplace (1806-07) for capillary theory; Gauss for the variational derivation (Principia generalia theoriae figurae fluidorum, 1830)

results.what: Call for advances in Geometria Situs
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz (term), Euler (1736), later Listing (1847) and Riemann

results.what: Equilibrium figure of a gaseous fluid mass without solid core
results.modern_name: Equilibrium figures of self-gravitating compressible (gaseous) bodies
results.usually_credited_to: Laplace (nebular context); later Lane (1870), Ritter, Emden (1907)

results.what: Mathematical theory of timbre (sound quality independent of pitch and loudness), especially the vowels of human speech
results.modern_name: Theory of timbre / vowel acoustics (Fourier analysis of waveform, formants)
results.usually_credited_to: Kratzenstein (1780 St Petersburg prize), Willis (1829), Ohm (1843), Helmholtz (1863)

results.what: Motion of an air bubble in a closed liquid-filled tube
results.modern_name: Bubble motion in confined tubes (two-phase hydrodynamics)
results.usually_credited_to: much later (e.g. Taylor bubbles, Davies & Taylor 1950)

deep.surprise_reason: The page only lists proposed problems, with no results. Gauss's interest in capillarity, geometria situs and cometary perturbations is well documented. The mildly notable detail is that around 1815-16 he explicitly framed timbre and vowel quality as a problem for mathematical theory. He separated it from pitch and loudness and anticipated the Ohm-Helmholtz programme by decades, but only as a question. The interest in a variational capillarity theory roughly 14 years before his 1830 memoir is also of minor biographical interest.
